newsitem.title: USA: Waigel - 1997 economic growth won't boost job growth.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - 1997 economic growth won't boost job growth.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Monday that expected growth in Germany's economy will fail to reduce unemployment noticeably.
In a speech to the Interim Committee of the International Monetary Fund, Waigel said, "The expected growth in 1997 will not be sufficient to noticeably reduce unemployment."
Waigel said that German unemployment is to a large extent structural and that fundamental reforms, including changes to the tax system, are needed.

Waigel repeated that he expects Germany's economy to grow 2.5 percent this year with continued low inflation, moderate wage increases and historically low interest rates contributing to a favorable economic environment.
The finance minister added that Germany will fulfill the criteria needed to qualify for European monetary union, and that the budget deficit will equal 2.9 percent of gross domestic product.
